transcript.content: Hi, welcome in. I'm Dr. [Name]. To start, can you tell me what's been bringing you in today?

Hello, Doctor. Well, I suppose what brings me in is that my sleep has become completely unmoored. 

At first, I was waking up after only two or three hours, and I'd be up drafting plans, just feeling completely ready to go. But lately... now I just lie awake before dawn. My stomach feels tight, and I get absolutely no sense of rest from it. It's just really taking a toll.

During that first phase when you were waking up after only two or three hours and felt ready to go, how would you describe your mood and energy during the day—did you feel unusually upbeat, confident, or 'wired' compared to your normal self?

Yes, I suppose 'upbeat' covers it. For a few weeks, I felt... almost brilliantly optimistic, really. It was like every obstacle in front of me was just completely trivial. I had all this energy to get things done. 

But, well, there was an edge to it, too. If anyone questioned my plans or what I was doing, I... I snapped at them. I got very short. It honestly felt like they were trying to sabotage me. I just felt like I was the only sensible man in the room, and everyone else was just dragging their feet and getting in my way.
Before this period of high energy, had you ever gone through a stretch of at least two weeks where you felt persistently sad, low, or lost interest in things you usually enjoy?

Yes, I did. Before that energetic phase, I went through a long stretch exactly like that. 

I used to spend whole afternoons at the museum, or I'd just lose myself in photography and cooking. I've always enjoyed those things. But during that low period... I would just look at my camera, or look at the bridge table, and I felt absolutely nothing. Well, nothing except the sheer effort it would take to even pretend I wanted to participate. It all just felt completely empty.
How many days in a row did that period of high energy, optimism, and irritability last?

I couldn't give you an exact number of days, to be honest. I know I mentioned earlier that it felt like it went on for a few weeks, but... well, I wasn't really keeping track of it day by day. It was just a continuous stretch for a while, and I'm not entirely sure exactly how long it lasted before it faded.

During that few weeks of high energy and optimism, did it cause any serious problems—like conflicts at work, financial or legal trouble, or anything that led others to become concerned about your behavior?

Yes, it did cause some serious issues. Um... well, my wife actually had to step in and take over our finances completely. She's also been staying with me pretty much all the time now, just for my safety. It's... a bit hard to admit that at my age, but it's the truth. 

And outside of the house, my usual commitments just fell apart. I stopped showing up reliably for the museum, and the arts council... I just wasn't there when I was supposed to be. Even with my friends, I just sort of dropped off the map. So, yes, my behavior definitely caused problems and made people concerned.

During that high-energy period, did you experience anything like hearing voices or seeing things others couldn't, or did you hold any beliefs—like having special powers, a special mission, or being targeted by others—that you later realized weren't true?

No, I didn't have anything like that. I didn't hear any voices or see anything that wasn't there. And I didn't think I had any special powers or missions or anything along those lines. It was just the energy and the racing thoughts, but no, none of those other things you mentioned.
Right now, over the past two weeks, have you been feeling persistently sad, down, or have you lost interest or pleasure in things you used to enjoy, like your photography or cooking?

Yes, I have. Um... I used to spend whole afternoons at the museum, or I'd just completely lose myself in my photography and cooking. But lately, I look at my camera or the bridge table and I feel absolutely nothing. There's just no interest there anymore. Really, the only thing I feel is just... the sheer effort it would take to even pretend to care about it.
In the past two weeks, have you had any thoughts of hurting yourself, or that life isn't worth living?

Well, yes. Honestly, there are mornings lately where I just... I think it would be a relief if I simply didn't wake up at all. It's gotten to the point where I actually frightened myself. That's why I told my wife that I shouldn't be left alone right now.
Right now, are you able to manage your usual daily activities—like getting dressed, eating regularly, or taking care of basic tasks—or has your depression made even these things very difficult?

Well, my wife has been helping me a lot with that. Honestly, it's a struggle just to get out of bed. Getting dressed, showering... it all feels like climbing a mountain. I haven't really been eating much either, unless she puts something right in front of me and encourages me to eat. I just don't have the energy for any of it.
